title: 3QBF
description: Assignments to the x-variables of an exists-forall-exists formula in conjunctive normal form that make it true: the standard Sigma-3-complete problem (Stockmeyer; Wrathall). Three solvers in a chain. The innermost solver reads the x-atoms too, so the link from B to C passes them on, and a second link from A to C turns the x-part of an unsat core into a clause for A.

fragments.name: shared
fragments.description: Added to every solver; the formula is in the Instances tab.
fragments.text: % The instance (its facts) is in the Instances tab.

fragments.name: outer
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): assignments to the x-variables.
fragments.text:
{ x(I) } :- xvar(I).
#show x/1.
% 'always' is true in every candidate; see the inner fragment.
{ always }.
:- not always.

fragments.name: glue_x
fragments.description: The interface atoms from A: the x-variables.

fragments.name: middle
fragments.description: Proposes a y-assignment (solver B); refined by the z-assignments that C finds.

fragments.name: glue_xy
fragments.description: The interface atoms from B to C: the y-variables and the x-variables that B received.

fragments.name: inner
fragments.description: Looks for a z-assignment that satisfies every clause under x and y (solver C).
fragments.text:
{ z(K) } :- zvar(K).
zsat(C) :- zlit(C,K,1), z(K).
zsat(C) :- zlit(C,K,0), not z(K).
% good(C,T): the interface atom T has the value that satisfies clause C.
good(C,x(I)) :- xlit(C,I,1), x(I).
good(C,x(I)) :- xlit(C,I,0), not x(I).
good(C,y(J)) :- ylit(C,J,1), y(J).
good(C,y(J)) :- ylit(C,J,0), not y(J).
ok(C) :- zsat(C).
ok(C) :- good(C,_).
% Every constraint reads 'always', so every unsat core contains it and is never empty.
:- clause(C), not ok(C), always.
#show z/1.

% z stays a witness while the clauses it does not satisfy itself keep their true
% x- and y-literals.
relevant(T) :- good(C,T), not zsat(C).
% If z satisfies every clause on its own, every candidate is a solution: blame 'always',
% and B has no y-assignment left.
open :- clause(C), not zsat(C).
relevant(always) :- not open.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + outer
solver B = shared + middle
solver C = shared + inner
link   GX  = A -> B via shared + glue_x
link   GXY = B -> C via shared + glue_xy
link   GXC = A -> C via shared + glue_x

# Three blocks: A proposes the x-assignment, B a y-assignment that might refute it, C a
# z-assignment that satisfies the clauses.
#   C finds z      -> y does not refute x; B learns a clause over the x- and y-atoms that
#                     z relies on (valid for every x, because the x-atoms are in it).
#   C finds none   -> y refutes x; A learns the x-part of the unsat core of C.
#   B has no y     -> every y has a z: the candidate is a solution.
# B runs as a search inside A's check (phase L2): its refinements stay between the candidates
# of A, so B needs far fewer solves than when it is solved again from scratch each time.
# 'keep Y' ends B's search at the first y that C cannot refute (Y is none when B is exhausted).
# GXY passes on the x-atoms that B received over GX, next to its own y-atoms. GXC is never
# used for assumptions: it lets GXC.core(C) state the x-part of the core as a clause for A.
search A:
    on candidate M:
        search B assume GX(M) keep Y:
            on candidate Y:
                W = C.solve(assume GXY(Y))
                if W: reject Y with GXY.clause(Y, W)
        if Y: reject M with GXC.core(C)

solver A = shared + outer
solver B = shared + middle
solver C = shared + inner
link   GX  = A -> B via shared + glue_x
link   GXY = B -> C via shared + glue_xy
link   GXC = A -> C via shared + glue_x

# Block-only baseline: B blocks each (x, y) that C answers, A each refuted x.
search A:
    on candidate M:
        search B assume GX(M) keep Y:
            on candidate Y:
                W = C.solve(assume GXY(Y))
                if W: reject Y with GXY.block(Y)
        if Y: reject M with GX.block(M)

solver A = shared + outer
solver B = shared + middle
solver C = shared + inner
link   GX  = A -> B via shared + glue_x
link   GXY = B -> C via shared + glue_xy
link   GXC = A -> C via shared + glue_x

# Three blocks: A proposes the x-assignment, B a y-assignment that might refute it, C a
# z-assignment that satisfies the clauses.
#   C finds z      -> y does not refute x; B learns a clause over the x- and y-atoms that
#                     z relies on (valid for every x, because the x-atoms are in it).
#   C finds none   -> y refutes x; A learns the x-part of the unsat core of C.
#   B has no y     -> every y has a z: the candidate is a solution.
# B runs as a search inside A's check (phase L2): its refinements stay between the candidates
# of A, so B needs far fewer solves than when it is solved again from scratch each time.
# 'keep Y' ends B's search at the first y that C cannot refute (Y is none when B is exhausted).
# GXY passes on the x-atoms that B received over GX, next to its own y-atoms. GXC is never
# used for assumptions: it lets GXC.core(C) state the x-part of the core as a clause for A.
search A:
    on candidate M:
        search B assume GX(M) keep Y:
            on candidate Y:
                W = C.solve(assume GXY(Y))
                if W: reject Y with GXY.clause(Y, W)
        if Y: reject M with C.core.minimal.on(GXC)

solver A = shared + outer
solver B = shared + middle
solver C = shared + inner
link   GX  = A -> B via shared + glue_x
link   GXY = B -> C via shared + glue_xy
link   GXC = A -> C via shared + glue_x

# B is solved again from scratch for every y (no inner search); its clauses stay.
search A:
    on candidate M:
        loop:
            Y = B.solve(assume GX(M))
            if not Y: break
            W = C.solve(assume GXY(Y))
            if W:
                B.add(GXY.clause(Y, W))
            else:
                reject M with GXC.core(C)
                break

instances.facts:
% exists x1..x4  forall y1..y3  exists z1..z3 :  C1 & ... & C10  (clauses of three literals)
% xlit(C,I,S): clause C contains x_I (S = 1) or its negation (S = 0); ylit/3, zlit/3 likewise.
xvar(1..4).  yvar(1..3).  zvar(1..3).  clause(1..10).
xlit(1,4,0). zlit(1,3,0). ylit(1,1,1).      % ~x4 v ~z3 v y1
zlit(2,2,1). ylit(2,1,0). xlit(2,1,1).      % z2 v ~y1 v x1
xlit(3,4,0). zlit(3,1,1). ylit(3,2,0).      % ~x4 v z1 v ~y2
ylit(4,2,0). zlit(4,3,1). xlit(4,4,1).      % ~y2 v z3 v x4
ylit(5,1,0). zlit(5,2,0). xlit(5,4,1).      % ~y1 v ~z2 v x4
ylit(6,1,1). zlit(6,3,0). xlit(6,3,1).      % y1 v ~z3 v x3
zlit(7,2,1). ylit(7,2,0). xlit(7,1,1).      % z2 v ~y2 v x1
ylit(8,2,1). zlit(8,3,1). xlit(8,3,1).      % y2 v z3 v x3
zlit(9,1,1). ylit(9,2,1). xlit(9,2,0).      % z1 v y2 v ~x2
ylit(10,3,0). zlit(10,3,1). xlit(10,2,1).   % ~y3 v z3 v x2

generators.name: qbf3-cnf
generators.description: A random exists-forall-exists QBF in CNF: c clauses of three literals over nx + ny + nz variables.
generators.text:
% qbf3-cnf: exists x1..x_nx forall y1..y_ny exists z1..z_nz : C1 & ... & Cc, three literals per clause.
% Each literal picks one of the nx + ny + nz variables uniformly and a sign with probability 1/2.
xvar(1..nx).
yvar(1..ny).
zvar(1..nz).
clause(1..c).
slot(1..3).
var(C,J,@int(1, nx+ny+nz, C, J)) :- clause(C), slot(J).
sign(C,J,@flip(500, C, J, sign)) :- clause(C), slot(J).
xlit(C,I,S) :- var(C,J,I), sign(C,J,S), I <= nx.
ylit(C,I-nx,S) :- var(C,J,I), sign(C,J,S), I > nx, I <= nx+ny.
zlit(C,I-nx-ny,S) :- var(C,J,I), sign(C,J,S), I > nx+ny.
#show xvar/1.
#show yvar/1.
#show zvar/1.
#show clause/1.
#show xlit/3.
#show ylit/3.
#show zlit/3.

library.summary: An exists-forall-exists formula: three solvers in a chain, clauses for the middle solver from witnesses and for the outer one from unsat cores (4 solutions).
